title: a discrete walkie-talkie bleep-bloop when the handset starts up (and the same asset is the natural PTT/roger beep later). Source picked by the owner: the FIRST SECOND of ~/Downloads/walkie-talkie-radio-signal-activation-bosnow-1-00-02.mp3 — trim it, encode to the device's Opus/Ogg or raw PCM, ship it with the app, play it once the audio route is up. Respect the silent position (volume knob off = screen off), and note the route is only guaranteed after audio-mixer verifies it (bq268-alpine)

wata's SetupMixer runs ONCE at startup (go-pkgs/audio/audio_linux.go), but the codec's controls reset to their defaults when the Q6 comes up or restarts — `RX2 MIX1 INP1` goes back to ZERO and the handset is silent with every other control still reading correct. bq268-alpine's audio-mixer service now applies-verifies-and-watches for 2 minutes, but a mid-SESSION Q6 restart would still silence the app until reboot. Cheap fix: re-assert the route (or at least verify the mux) when a playback stream is opened — note mixer_open enumerates ~700 controls and is too slow mid-stream, so use a pre-opened handle like VolCtl

exiting wata on the handset should offer a menu instead of just quitting: relaunch the app / reboot / poweroff / reboot to fastboot / reboot to EDL. Fastboot and EDL each need a second confirmation (they leave the device unusable to its user until someone with a cable intervenes). title: live arrival could NOT be reproduced (2026-08-07) — six configurations all deliver it: control send, a 90s-idle session, ACROSS a server restart, arrival while the CONVERSATION IS OPEN (that one is now a permanent mac-smoke case, it was the real oracle gap), over localhost TCP and over iroh. The windowed-pump theory is also out: `frame` is shared verbatim with the headless pump and macshell.Apply hops to the main queue. What is NOT ruled out: a session open for HOURS (only 90s was tested), and the owner's build being older than the server it ran against. Both clients now log `have: +Ns conv=N msgs=N unplayed=N conn=…` on every change plus a 60s heartbeat, so the next occurrence is decisive: a count standing still under conn=syncing is a sync bug, a moving count that never reaches the screen is a rendering bug. REOPEN with that log, do not re-derive this list
